thread:
Priya Nair: Heads-up: cost dashboard showing spikes for org 8201 in several customers' dashboards. Noticed when supporting a customer call — they saw another org's quota burn.

Alex Gomez: whoa. repro steps? a screenshot would help.

Priya Nair: screenshot pasted (redacted). Steps: open Settings -> Usage -> per-route chart. Select customer A (org 4302) and timeframe last 24h. Top row shows usage tag org=8201.

Li Wang: could be tag normalization bug in telemetry export. We recently switched exporter to batch-mode which flattens labels. Did we rename header mapping?

Tom Bowers: related PR #560 renamed "X-Customer" -> "X-Org-Id" in internal-api. Some downstream services still read X-Customer and fallback to session lookup. If telemetry uses the wrong header during attribution it could map to the session's org (stale).

Priya Nair: pasted debug trace: 
```
POST /internal/usage
headers: {"X-Cust": "8201", "Cookie": "session=abcd"}
payload: {"route": "/api/chat", "tokens": 234}
```
But telemetry DB row has org_id=4302.

Alex Gomez: that implies an overwrite between request handling and telemetry ingestion. Maybe the request pipeline normalizes `org` from session if header present but wrong name. We also recently cached session->org mapping in redis with 5m TTL. If a worker picked wrong session id could swap.

Li Wang: we should add an ingest-time guard: if incoming header exists, prefer it and emit a mismatch metric when DB attribute differs. Example pseudo: 
```
let incoming = headers['x-org-id'] || headers['x-cust']
if (dbRow.org != incoming) { emit('telemetry.attr_mismatch', {expected: incoming, seen: dbRow.org}) }
```

Tom Bowers: careful: many internal paths rely on session fallback. For safety, do sampling-only first. If mismatch > 0.2% for 1h then auto-block the fallback and reject with 422 so caller must retry with explicit header.

Priya Nair: agreed. Also add a one-off backfill to find historical misattrib windows. Billing team will need accurate windows to reconcile invoices.

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-912: investigate possible misattribution windows; assigned to @Tom Bowers.

deploy-bot: CI deploy rolling: telemetry-exporter v2.4.1 -> canary 10% at 2026-03-21T14:05.

Alex Gomez: action list: 1) Li to add `telemetry.attr_mismatch` counter + dashboard 2) Tom to open BILL ticket & check session cache TTL / eviction 3) Priya to run backfill query to find likely windows 4) Alex to prepare a small middleware patch for sampling-only mismatch checks.

Li Wang: I'll add a Grafana panel and an alert: `sum(telemetry_attr_mismatch)/sum(telemetry_ingested) > 0.001` -> page to #eng-platform if fires.

Tom Bowers: re: root cause hunt: I'll pull router logs for last 48h and correlates canary rollout windows. If we see affinity churn correlated with the time ranges it supports the routing-flip theory.

Priya Nair: customers notified? I pinged support to hold off on billing adjustments until we confirm magnitude. Also flagged Legal for any SLA exposure.

Alex Gomez: small note: ensure we don't log PII in the mismatch logs (session ids only, no user email). We'll scrub in code.

Priya Nair: thanks all. If anyone sees a spike post-canary roll ping this thread with trace ids. We'll reconvene after Li's dashboard is live. :yess:
